primary_task: Interactively set up a goal, metric command and scope with the user, then autonomously edit code, commit, run the metric command, and keep or revert each experiment in a git repo.

requirements.name: git
requirements.evidence: compatibility: Requires git. The project must be a git repository.
requirements.basis: bash: ... build, test, run CLIs and scripts, git, gh, start and stop local servers inside the session

requirements.name: terminal/shell
requirements.evidence: Requires terminal access to run commands.
requirements.basis: A Claude Code cloud session on Linux x86_64 ... with a shell

requirements.name: interactive user conversation for setup
requirements.evidence: Ask the user directly for each item. Do not assume or skip any.
requirements.basis: ask_user: ask the user a question (with options) and read the answer in the conversation

requirements.name: user-defined METRIC_COMMAND and its dependencies
requirements.evidence: The command to run (e.g., `dotnet test`, `npm run benchmark`, `time ./build.sh`, `pytest --tb=short`)
requirements.basis: The manifest cannot decide; the metric command is chosen by the user. It is blocked only if it needs a GPU, Docker or a refused host

notes: Generic loop; status depends on the user's metric command, which is unknown. Rule 10 forbids installing dependencies without approval, so installable programs need user consent. Experiments are committed and reset locally (no push). The loop runs until interrupted, which a cloud session may cut short; not a manifest item. If the user picks a GPU training metric (the doc cites VRAM/OOM and learning-rate examples), it would be BLOCKED on hardware:GPU.
